simple.meaning: שְׁזַב (shᵉzab) appears 9 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced in connection with kingship.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in Daniel, beginning at Daniel 3:15. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as Torah, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שְׁזַב (H7804) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows שְׁזַב through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.
simple.summary: שְׁזַב (shᵉzab) / H7804 is tracked through Daniel 3:15, Daniel 3:17, Daniel 3:28, Daniel 6:15. The entry is generated from source alignment, occurrence evidence, and the surrounding Scripture context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Now if you are ready whenever you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music to fall down and worship the image which I have made, good; but if you don’t worship, you shall be cast the same hour into the middle of a burning fiery furnace. Who is that god that will deliver you out of my hands?”

timeline.evidenceText: Now if you are ready whenever you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music to fall down and worship the image which I have made, good; but if you don’t worship, you shall be cast the same hour into the middle of a burning fiery furnace. Who is that god that will deliver you out of my hands?”
If it happens, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace; and he will deliver us out of your hand, O king.
If it happens, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace; and he will deliver us out of your hand, O king.

Nebuchadnezzar spoke and said, “Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who has sent his angel, and delivered his servants who trusted in him, and have changed the king’s word, and have yielded their bodies, that they might not serve nor worship any god, except their own God.
Then these men assembled together to the king, and said to the king, “Know, O king, that it is a law of the Medes and Persians, that no decree nor statute which the king establishes may be changed.”
A stone was brought, and laid on the mouth of the den; and the king sealed it with his own signet, and with the signet of his lords; that nothing might be changed concerning Daniel.
Then Daniel said to the king, “O king, live forever!
So this Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius, and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian.

definitions.full: H7804. shezab or shezib שֵׁיזִב verb deliver (probably Shaph`el as loan-word from Assyrian šûzub(u), ušêib , deliver , √ ezêbu ( א 4 = עזב ), Dl Pr 140 Hpt GGN 1583, 91 ; BAS i.13 K § 43, l, Anm .; שֵׁיזֵב ᵑ7 , Syriac , Christian-Palestinian Aramaic Schulth Lex. 203 , also Nabataean שיזב Cooke 255 ; compare proper name מְשֵׁיזַבְאֵל Biblical Hebrew; Old Aramaic צלמשזב SAC 102 ; see also following article); — Perfect 3masculine singular שֵׁיזִב Dan 3:28 ; 6:28 ; Imperfect 3masculine singular יְשֵׁיזִ֑ב 3:17 ; suffix יְשֵׁיזְבִנָּךְ 6:17 , נְִ֯כבוֺן 3:13 ; Infinitive suffix לְשֵׁיזָבוּתָךְ 6:21 , הֵתּ - 6:15 , תַ֑נָּא - 3:17 ; — deliver (usually with מִן ): 3:17 b, ל accusative of person 3:28 ; 6:28 b, suffix person 3:15 , 17 a; 6:15 ; 6:17 ; 6:21 , absolute 6:28 a.
